title: Open-Crumb Rustic Italian Ciabatta
summary: A very wet dough built on an overnight starter, with a splash of milk for a softer crumb, is strengthened by folding, shaped gently into two flat slipper loaves and baked on a hot stone.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle and dough hook
large square container or bowl, oiled
baking stone or heavy upturned baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Starter
steps.text: Mix the starter and leave it 8-24 hours.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Beat the dough until the wet mixture pulls away in ribbons.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold in the container every 30 minutes during the first hour of a 2-hour rise.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn out, halve and press gently into slipper shapes, then rest.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Dimple and bake on the stone until golden and 96 °C.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool for an hour so the crumb sets.

tips: The dough should be too wet to knead by hand; that is what makes the holes.
Handle it as little as possible when shaping so the bubbles survive.
Use plenty of flour on the worktop and your hands.
storage: Keep in a paper bag for up to 2 days and crisp in a hot oven, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
